explanation: Let dp[v] count ordered sequences totaling v. Try every candidate as the final value and add dp[v minus candidate]. BigInteger avoids intermediate overflow before the contract's int-sized final count.
timeComplexity: O(target times c) arithmetic operations for c candidates; big-integer costs depend on count width.
spaceComplexity: O(target) BigInteger cells, plus their count bit storage.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: A sequence totaling v has one final candidate c and a preceding sequence totaling v-c. Grouping sequences by that last value partitions them into disjoint cases. Adding dp[v-c] across candidates therefore counts every ordered sequence exactly once, with dp[0]=1 for the empty sequence.
walkthrough: For candidates [2,3] and target 7, the only multiset is two 2s and one 3. Its orders are [2,2,3],[2,3,2],[3,2,2], so return 3. These orders count separately, unlike Combination Sum.
edgeCases: Target zero has one empty ordered sequence.
Arbitrary-precision intermediate counts avoid overflow before the int-sized final result.
